sources.title: SUSY Breaking at the Tip of Throat and Mirage Mediation

evidence.text: Stabilize heavy fields, estimate their auxiliary components, eliminate fluctuations and insert their vacuum values into light couplings. Here S, U, X and Z are removed while the Goldstino, T and C remain.

sources.title: Classical and Quantum SUSY Breaking Effects in IIB Local Models

evidence.text: Expand the supergravity potential at large volume; compute moduli F-terms and matter-metric sectional curvatures; insert them into the supergravity soft-mass formula. The universal-mass calculation retains F^s contributions and subleading curvature terms important for its sign.

sources.title: Anomalous U(1) Mediation in Large Volume Compactification

evidence.text: Appendix A diagonalizes the component mass spectrum and evaluates its one-loop supertrace potential. The paper uses this calculation to identify the negative scalar threshold and match the cutoff-superfield dependence used in the superspace treatment.

sources.title: Sequestered de Sitter String Scenarios: Soft-terms

evidence.text: Compute moduli F-terms and gravity-mediated gaugino, scalar, trilinear and Higgs-bilinear terms, including relevant D-terms and subleading no-scale corrections. The authors developed the Mathematica package LargeVol for potential minimization and soft-term calculations.

sources.title: Large-volume flux compactifications: Moduli spectrum and D3/D7 soft supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Dimensional reduction and volume power counting organize higher-derivative corrections. Moduli masses are extracted from potential derivatives after approximate canonical normalization near the minimum.

sources.title: Soft SUSY Breaking Terms for Chiral Matter in IIB String Compactifications

evidence.text: Evolve string-scale boundary conditions using SoftSUSY2.0; use micrOmegas1.3 for relic density and flavour observables, and scan charge/colour-breaking directions including UFB3. These are historical phenomenological calculations.

evidence.text: How do the characteristics and stabilization of anomalous-U(1) D-flat directions determine the relative contributions of modulus, gauge, anomaly and D-term mediation in vacua with nearly vanishing cosmological constant?

evidence.text: How do vacuum branches, bare cosmological constants and D7-brane soft supersymmetry-breaking parameters change when the flux superpotential W₀ is varied over approximately twenty orders of magnitude without uplift terms?

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking and moduli stabilization with anomalous U(1) gauge symmetry

sources.title: The $F$-term Problem and other Challenges of Stringy Quintessence

evidence.text: An additional brane-sector F-term can raise observable-sector superpartner masses independently of the small Kähler-mediated scale. The same auxiliary expectation also carries vacuum energy, so lowering the mediation scale becomes relevant to the cosmological obstruction.

destination.title: Sequestering, bulk exchange and flavor
destination.question: Under what conditions do brane separation or local compactification structure suppress unwanted soft terms and flavor violation, and when do bulk couplings obstruct that suppression?
destination.summary: Keeps conditional sequestering proposals separate from tests of genericity and from bounds on bulk-field masses.

systems: Supersymmetric compactifications with propagating bulk fields
targets: Suppression of tree-level and bulk-mediated contributions
Conditions for anomaly or gaugino mediation to dominate
assumptions: Spatial separation alone is not adopted as sufficient
Light bulk fields do not by themselves prove failure when their couplings are specially constrained
Asymmetric compactifications require separate scale comparisons
excludes: Anomaly dominance inferred solely from locality

sources.title: Brane world SUSY breaking

evidence.text: Study corrections by evaluating a probe Dp-brane DBI action in a source Dp′-brane metric and dilaton background, and by reviewing the heterotic Calabi-Yau expansion of bulk fields in ε = T/S.

sources.title: Out of this world supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Use separated-brane position-space propagators and dimensional analysis to estimate finite bulk-loop soft masses. Heavy bulk exchange is exponentially suppressed by propagation across the compact dimension.

sources.title: Brane world SUSY breaking

evidence.text: Use extended supersymmetry to fix the leading Kähler potential and use T-duality and type-I–heterotic duality to relate brane realizations. For Hořava-Witten/T6, the potential is a logarithm of a determinant involving moduli and both branes' matter bilinears, plus the dilaton logarithm.

sources.title: Brane world SUSY breaking

evidence.text: Trace effective brane couplings to Chern-Simons-squared interactions: wall sources for the eleven-dimensional three-form generate bulk four-form strength, while a type-I′ description uses exchange of the bulk Ramond two-form.

sources.title: Out of this world supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Isolate the supergravity scalar auxiliary background, rescale visible chiral fields, and track super-Weyl and Konishi anomalies through cutoff-dependent couplings. Expand wavefunction renormalization in the background superfield; Appendix B illustrates the mechanism with regulated SQED.

evidence.text: Estimate radiative masses through superspace effective operators containing a Higgs insertion and a supersymmetry-breaking F-term. Dimensional analysis uses the leading hidden-field case n=0 and distinguishes mediation from loop-particle scales.

sources.title: Radiative Fermion Masses in Local D-Brane Models

evidence.text: Transform the Yukawa matrix to a mass basis using ATYB=D, with YY† and Y†Y determining the transformations. Track gauge and global charges of the mass eigenstates to identify forbidden light-generation mass terms.

evidence.text: Use the Runge Higgs basis to separate the VEV-carrying Higgs from orthogonal flavour-changing Higgses. Estimate extra-Higgs and gluino–squark loop mechanisms and compare flavour-changing interactions with neutral-meson constraints.
